correlates.name: AV Block (Heart Block)
correlates.presentation: PR interval >200 ms. Degrees range from first through third; third-degree (complete) block shows complete atrioventricular dissociation, with the ventricles escaping at a rate unrelated to the atria.
correlates.pathophysiology: impaired conduction through the AV node or the infranodal system. Because the PR interval is the electrical time spent traversing the AV node, nodal disease lengthens it.

correlates.name: Potassium Disorders on the ECG
correlates.presentation: hyperkalemia raises T wave amplitude and can also widen the QRS; hypokalemia flattens the T wave and brings out a U wave, which looks like an inverted T wave sitting after it.
correlates.pathophysiology: serum potassium sets the repolarization gradient, so it is read off the T wave.

correlates.name: ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
correlates.presentation: chest pain, discomfort or pressure - the trigger phrase for "EKG, stat" to rule out acute coronary syndrome.
correlates.pathophysiology: transmural ischemia shifts the injured myocardium's resting potential, lifting the ST segment.

correlates.name: Congenital Long QT Syndrome and Torsades de Pointes
correlates.presentation: may be silent until syncope or arrest; the family history is the clue - sudden cardiac death in relatives.
correlates.pathophysiology: prolonged ventricular repolarization from a congenital channelopathy, an electrolyte imbalance, or a drug (Slide 12).

findings.name: P Wave
findings.represents: The summation of right and left atrial depolarization, with the left atrium depolarizing slightly later than the right
findings.territory: Atria — assessed in the money leads II, III, aVF and V1
findings.association: A double hump (P mitrale) means one atrium is enlarged or intra-atrial conduction is delayed; a tall P wave means atrial hypertrophy

findings.name: PR Interval
findings.represents: The time from the onset of atrial depolarization to the onset of ventricular depolarization — essentially conduction time through the AV node
findings.territory: AV node, the deliberate delay between atrial and ventricular contraction
findings.association: Prolonged beyond one large box in first-, second- and third-degree AV block; normal is 120-200 ms

findings.name: QRS Complex
findings.represents: Ventricular depolarization — Q is the first downstroke, R the upstroke, S the second downstroke
findings.territory: Ventricular myocardium and the His-Purkinje system
findings.association: Widened beyond 120 ms by bundle branch or fascicular block, hyperkalemia, tricyclic antidepressants, sodium channel blockers and WPW

findings.name: ST Segment
findings.represents: The interval when the ventricles are fully depolarized and mechanically contracting, so no net current flows
findings.territory: Localizes the injured wall by which contiguous leads are involved
findings.association: Elevation in two or more contiguous leads defines a STEMI; depression signals subendocardial ischemia

findings.name: T Wave
findings.represents: Ventricular repolarization — the lecturer's line is that potassium lives under the T wave
findings.association: Peaked and narrow in hyperkalemia; flattened with a following U wave in hypokalemia

findings.name: QT Interval
findings.represents: Depolarization through repolarization — the electrical equivalent of ventricular systole
findings.association: Prolongation from congenital long QT syndrome, electrolyte derangement or the anti-ABCDE drugs risks torsades de pointes; normal is 0.36-0.44 s and under half the R-R interval

findings.name: TP Segment
findings.represents: Electrical rest during diastole, from the end of the T wave to the start of the next P wave
findings.association: The true isoelectric reference line — ST elevation and depression are measured against it, not against the PR segment

findings.name: R Wave Progression
findings.represents: The R wave growing steadily more positive from V1 through V3, with the transition to a dominant R between V3 and V4
findings.territory: Sweeping across the precordium from septum to lateral wall
findings.association: Poor progression is a marker of anterior infarction or lead misplacement; normal progression is a marker of heart health

findings.name: Delta Wave
findings.represents: A slurred upstroke at the start of the QRS from pre-excitation through an accessory pathway that bypasses the AV node
findings.territory: Accessory bundle bridging atrium and ventricle
findings.association: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome — a short PR with a widened QRS

formulas.name: Normal ECG Intervals
formulas.equation: PR 120-200 ms; QRS < 120 ms; QT < half the R-R interval
formulas.meaning: The three interval judgments that anchor every ECG read — AV nodal conduction, ventricular depolarization, and total ventricular systole
formulas.normalValue: 1 small box = 0.04 s, 1 large box = 0.2 s; QT 0.36-0.44 s

formulas.name: Intrinsic Pacemaker Rates
formulas.meaning: The SA node is dominant and defines bradycardia below 60 and tachycardia above 100; the AV node takes over as an escape pacemaker at a slower intrinsic rate
formulas.normalValue: Conduction velocity order: Purkinje > atria > ventricles > AV node

formulas.name: Normal Electrical Axis
formulas.equation: -30 to +60 degrees, assessed with leads I and aVF
formulas.meaning: The mean direction of ventricular depolarization, which points down and to the left because the left ventricle is thicker; I and aVF are used because they are perpendicular
formulas.normalValue: Both leads upright is normal; I up with aVF down is left axis deviation, I down with aVF up is right axis deviation
